Then Abu Taghlib showed many kindnesses to the Domesticus,
in order to confirm friendship with the Romans.
Now it happened that a malignant ulcer broke out on that Domesticus,
and he died there.
And in this year,
the people of Baghdad, when they heard of the captivity and slaughter that had occurred in Nisibis, became zealous,
and made a great uproar against the Caliph,
that is, al-Muti‘.
And they mocked him,
as one who was neglectful of the fight on behalf of the Arabs {Muslims},
and they even shot arrows into his palace and at his servants.
Moreover, some notable men went to the Emir ‘Izz al-Dawlah, who had gone to Kufa,
and incited him to send an army against the Romans.
And in the year 363
[363] of the Arabs,
al-Muti‘, king of the Arabs,
that is, the Caliph,
suffered a stroke of paralysis,
and his tongue became heavy,
and his movement ceased.
Therefore, one of the magnates of Baghdad, whose name was Sabuktakin, forced him,
and he abdicated,
and handed over the realm to his son, who was called al-Ta'i‘.
And in this same year died the physician Thabit ibn Sinan ibn Thabit, the pagan of Harran.
And this man wrote the famous book of chronicles,
from the year two hundred and ninety of the Arabs down to the end of his days.
And had it not been for him,
most of the affairs of the Arab kings would have been lost and forgotten;
but he preserved them,
and they were transmitted to the chroniclers who arose after him.
After al-Muti‘, al-Ta'i‘ reigned over it {the realm} seventeen years and nine months.
When this man became king,
he magnified Sabuktakin, who had made him king,
and gave him the title of Nasir al-Dawlah.
And strife fell among the people,
because the Sunni Arabs and the Turks were with Sabuktakin,
while the Shiite Arabs and the Daylamites were with ‘Izz al-Dawlah.
And many were killed in the midst {of the city},
and great mansions were plundered.
And in the year 364
[364] of the Arabs,
which is the year 1286
[1286] of the Greeks
([975] of our Lord),
John (Ioannes), king of the Romans, that is, Tzimiskes, marched out to Syria,
and took control of Homs and Baalbek.
